title: Structural reductions toward the quartic Hessian conjecture in dimension four
oneLine: Exact certificates narrow a degree-five repeated-factor boundary of full HC4—the all-degree Hessian Conjecture in four variables—without proving secant closure, full HC4 or JC2.
abstract: This anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed computer-assisted candidate packages exact structural reductions for a degree-five boundary of the unrestricted four-dimensional Hessian Conjecture (full HC4). Here full HC4 quantifies over four-variable polynomial potentials of every finite degree. Ni's arXiv:2608.14217v1 claims the degree-at-most-four case; the present release starts from a ternary quintic normal layer h5 and therefore addresses a degree-five branch not covered by that preprint. It excludes every clean binary-decimic restriction with exactly five support points, proves that all 31 generators of the multiplicity-six binary-decimic locus vanish on the tangent normal layer, and gives three exact rational localized-colon elements on the unresolved secant chart. A prospectively selected 16-column experiment then lifts through 173^4, reconstructs all 585,392 coordinates uniquely over the rationals, replays against 85,688 equations, and passes a separate direct-polynomial audit. The closing result is a source-kernel theorem, not membership of the inhomogeneous fourth target. Secant-orbit closure, colon equality, saturation, fourth-target membership, full HC4 and JC2 remain open. Internal five-role review passed after repair, but unaffiliated reproduction, formal verification, external specialist review and peer review have not occurred.
narration: A quartic Hessian problem in four variables is one of the first unresolved cases in a route toward the Jacobian conjecture. This Evidence Press release does not solve that problem. It makes one difficult boundary smaller and more explicit. First, exact characteristic-zero certificates exclude the case where the associated binary decimic has exactly five distinct roots. Second, on the tangent residual orbit, every one of the thirty-one equations defining the multiplicity-six target is proved to vanish on the clean normal layer. The remaining secant orbit is harder. There the release proves three successive rational colon identities, but not the full saturation. The closing experiment asks whether sixteen prospectively chosen sparse source directions survive exact lifting. They do: four characteristic-one-hundred-and-seventy-three solves lift the batch through the fourth p-adic digit, all five hundred and eighty-five thousand three hundred and ninety-two coordinates reconstruct uniquely, every matrix row replays, and a separate implementation expands all sixteen rational combinations to the zero polynomial. This is a positive structural signal, not fourth-target membership. The paper, full ZIP, exact receipts, failed routes, review record and replay scripts are public under DOI 10.5281/zenodo.22216400. This is the anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed version 0.1.0 candidate, published 1 September 2026. The voice is synthetic, and this briefing is a communication aid, not additional evidence.

evidence: A 10-page manuscript and accessible Markdown; seven machine-readable claim units; exact characteristic-zero certificates for seven five-support partitions and all 31 tangent target generators; three rational colon identities; a frozen 85,688 by 36,587 integer matrix interface; four canonical 16-right-hand-side LinBox solves; unique rational reconstruction of 585,392 coordinates from 173^4; exact row replay and a direct-polynomial replay with sixteen zero residuals; a complete 1,180-file manifest; failed and inconclusive recovery receipts; a five-role producer-coordinated internal review, response matrix and bounded confirmation; clean-extraction replay; and byte-identical GitHub and Zenodo ZIP and PDF assets. These establish availability, producer-side replay, integrity and the stated bounded results—not fourth-target membership, secant closure, HC4, JC2, independent reproduction or peer review.
statusDetail: Anonymous, AI-assisted, unrefereed computer-assisted structural-reductions candidate. Full HC4 means the Hessian Conjecture for four-variable polynomial potentials of arbitrary finite degree. Ni's unrefereed arXiv:2608.14217v1 claims the degree-at-most-four case; this release's ternary-quintic h5 construction lies in the degree-five frontier and neither proves nor refutes Ni's theorem candidate. The exact five-support, tangent-orbit, colon-element and 16-column source-kernel claims have producer-side rational or characteristic-zero replay. The direct-polynomial audit bypasses the sparse row encoding but remains producer-coordinated. The 16-column selection rule was frozen before transfer computation. A fixed-gauge fourth target lifts through 173^96, but rational recovery failed under the preregistered hierarchy; this is not evidence of non-membership. No unaffiliated rerun, independent reimplementation, proof-assistant formalization, external specialist review, journal peer review, absolute priority determination or impact evaluation has occurred. The release does not prove full HC4 or JC2.
